notes:
## 0.2.271

owes: none — `bootHub` is split into storage, settings, the stores, one builder per module bundle and the listeners (SPEC-187 §8, REV-HUB-03): a move, not a rewrite; the start order, the start-up lines, the routes and the plugins are unchanged.
owes: none — the DataCore 0.5.39 re-pin's API changes are taken (stocks `SharedQuoteMapper.toRecord` is nullable, tennis mappers take the body text and `SharedKeys.authority` is `addressWithoutScheme`): the hub reads the same bodies and writes the same rows, except that a shared quote holding a NaN or infinite number is not written. The re-pin line above said the interval owed nothing; it owed these.
owes: none — the guide's certificate chapter names browsers by role (SPEC-187 §4): the five `guide/README-<lang>.md` copies are taken again from the documentation repository at `aad14d8`, wording only.
owes: a changed default (SPEC-187 §1, §2, DECISIONS 47) — a present `SYNCHUB_ALLOWED_HOSTS` now wins over the stored list at every start, as `SYNCHUB_EGRESS_ALLOW_HOSTS`, `SYNCHUB_ARTICLE_RETENTION_DAYS`, `SYNCHUB_UPDATE_CHECK` and `SYNCHUB_ARTICLE_TEXT_MAX_BYTES` do: an operator who set it in `compose.yml` and later changed the list on Settings → Setup finds the `compose.yml` value back after the update, with one start-up line naming both. Leave the variable out to keep the stored list editable. A field whose variable is present is drawn read-only with the variable's name, a write to it stores nothing (the page says why), and `/api/v1/settings` marks the row `"locked": true` and answers `409 {"error":"set_by_environment"}` to a write (the engine and SyncDesk read the extra row flag, which older ones ignore). The hint `setup.reachability.envWins` is gone, replaced by `setup.reachability.envLocked`. No migration, no new key.
owes: a migration (SPEC-173 §7) — V040 adds `devices.awaiting_confirmation` (existing devices read 0), and an earlier release cannot open the database afterwards; a rollback needs the backup taken before the update. A pairing delegated by a paired device that ends at `full` now waits for the account to allow it on Settings → Devices (*Allow* / *Refuse*, an amber dot on *Settings*): until then its token reaches only `GET /hub/status`, which adds `"awaitingConfirmation": true`, and every other device route answers `403 {"error":"confirmation_pending"}`. A delegation that ends at `backup` stays one tap. A waiting device counts toward no sweep floor, *App sync* dot or paired-app list.
owes: SyncDesk and the phone apps — `uiModel` 21 (SPEC-173 §7): `DeviceFact.awaitingConfirmation` and the Devices body's delegation card (`devices.delegation.title|from|gain|allow|refuse` in the engine zip's `ui-strings/`), the actions `devices.delegationAllow` and `devices.delegationRefuse` with the engine relays of the same names (`POST /api/v1/devices/own/{id}/delegation/allow|refuse`), and `awaitingConfirmation` on the `/api/v1/devices/own` rows; SyncDesk raises its floor to 21 and draws the card. SyncCore and AppShell read `confirmation_pending` and `awaitingConfirmation` so a full delegated pairing waits for the browser instead of reading as a fault.
owes: a migration (SPEC-194) — V039 adds `records.written_at` (the hub's clock at each write, backfilled from `updated_at` clamped to now), and an earlier release cannot open the database afterwards, so a rollback needs the backup taken before the update. Tombstones are kept 30 days from when the hub wrote them, not from the pushing device's `updatedAt`: a deletion pushed late now survives its full 30 days. No wire change, so no consumer owes anything; no configuration key.
owes: SyncDesk — `uiModel` 20 (SPEC-193): `BackupAppRow` (`label`, `icon`) is a new row kind, drawn as a chip; a `card` section now carries an `icon` and a `note` on the App backups page, which lists one card per app that holds a backup, the grand total only with two or more apps, and one last *Not backed up yet* card; the engine zip's `ui-strings/` gains `appBackups.notYet.title` and drops `appBackups.noneForApp`. SyncDesk raises its floor to 20 (it needs SPEC-192's 19 first). No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.
owes: SyncDesk — `uiModel` 19 (SPEC-192 §4): a `Group` gains `toggle` (default `false`), and `readerViewCommands` marks the `showRead` group a toggle group of two options, the first on; a renderer that does not know the field still draws the two options, but SyncDesk refuses an engine above its floor, so it raises its floor to 19 and draws a toggle group as one switch (SyncDesk SPEC-33). No migration, no configuration key, no wire change, no `ui-strings/` change; the web pages draw Settings → Apps, Settings → Interface → *Slide* and the `⋮` panel's *Show read* as a switch instead of buttons.
owes: none — DataCore's `feed`, `weather`, `stocks`, `notes` and `tennis` cores re-pinned from 0.5.38 to 0.5.39, whose interval owes this repository nothing; build files only, no behaviour change.
owes: SyncDesk — `uiModel` 18 (SPEC-191): `InstantStyle.DAY` is a new enum value (the day and month in the page's language, `6 October` / `17 August 2014`; an older SyncDesk fails to read `"day"`), the notes' `NoteRow` gains `untitled`, `items` (`NoteRowItem`), `checkedHidden`, `meta` and `conflict` with defaults, `Block.NoteEditor` gains `progress` and `age`, `NoteItem` gains `due` and `overdue`, and the icon tokens `pushPin`, `checkBoxBlank`, `checkBox`, `arrowUp` and `arrowDown` are new; the engine zip's `ui-strings/` gains `notes.others.title`, `notes.checkedHidden.*`, `notes.item.overdue`, `notes.conflict.chip`, `notes.status.savedAgo` and `notes.editor.attachmentsCount`. The engine's `excerpt` is unchanged (still the 160-character one-line text). No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: SyncDesk — `uiModel` 17 (SPEC-195 §2): the weather accuracy card's collecting state carries its progress (`AccuracyCardFact.collectingCounted`, `collectingScoredOn`), the stalled hint (`collectingStalled`, `lastReadingAgoMillis`) and the city for its sensor link (`placeId`); the engine zip's `ui-strings/` gains `weather.accuracy.collectingCounted`, `collectingNoReading`, `collectingSensorLink` and `collectingStalled`, and rewords `collectingDated` (*Archiving forecasts since …*, first figures one day later). The first scoring after the update re-reads days an earlier build dropped, so a calm sensor's figures can appear a night later. No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.
